rules.dedupe: Collapse framework/rendering repeats, repeated stages of one figure family, and architecture examples with the same operation/role graph. Record every alternative brief and the preserved distinctions under alsoCovers and dedupeBasis. Different normalization, gating, cache, or routing operations stay separate.
rules.priority: Phase-02-linked families first by earliest explicit lesson; transformer/attention next; remaining figures last. Topic coherence breaks ties within the latter two bands. A representative with an explicit lesson link wins over an unlinked alias.
rules.topicPlacement: The earliest explicit lesson determines a linked family's primary topic for the requested tranche order; all other source lesson links remain metadata. Unlinked families use their content topic.
rules.smallTopics: Forward-merge topics with fewer than four candidates into the next topic in the same priority band, recording the exception, original slugs and modules. Each resulting batch has one named data release. Split larger groups into balanced batches of at most twelve.
rules.sourceKinds: Kinds are the union of the source briefs' tags, not a drafted panels spec. In particular comparison here often means a side-by-side layout, not the renderer's text-column comparison kind.
rules.scope: Only the union of the supplied two lists. The ten numeric-only entries are explicitly in scope; no other single-kind figures or gaps.md tail figures are added.
rules.hold: Stop at this queue. The owner must approve the queue and each batch's ids/keywords; authored specs also require the owner-supplied explain/composition SHA.

estimateNote: 134 families is four above the rough 100–130 estimate. The extra distinctions are retained rather than conflating normalization placement, cache/index reuse, residual state, or expert-routing mechanisms.

references.dedupeBasis: Local opening followed by separate fine/coarse history reads; keep the two history roles.

references.summary: Block-level sparse attention can read all visible positions in the current partial block and a selected subset of completed blocks.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 101; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Selected old blocks plus legal current-block positions, with fragment lookup and residual gate kept distinct.

references.summary: A decoder can use a nearby window in most layers and a retrieved shortlist in the rest without doing full attention anywhere.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 108; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Window band versus retrieved shortlist without any full-attention layers.

references.summary: Latent bottlenecks compress the query and the cached key/value state separately within a mixed decoder.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 110; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Query compression and key/value-cache compression are separate projections.

references.summary: Latent experts can work at a narrower width and have their outputs normalized before the routed outputs are combined.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 111; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Per-expert normalization before routed combination with no shared expert branch.

references.summary: A decoder can combine sparse experts, residual scaling, and a bounded scoring head without conflating their purposes.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 113; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Bounded scoring curve and residual scaling are different mechanisms from expert routing.

references.summary: A decoder can combine windowed attention with learned sink scores and still use global attention on some layers.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 115; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Learned sink score is separate from ordinary local/global token access.

references.summary: A hybrid decoder can handle most layers with gated state updates and use attention in selected layers.
references.sequence: Gated-state hybrid baseline

alsoCovers.summary: A hybrid stack can mix token history mainly through a carried state and invoke attention only at selected depths.
alsoCovers.sequence: State-space and expert hybrid baseline

alsoCovers.summary: Irregularly grouped state and attention layers can all feed one style of sparse token update.
alsoCovers.sequence: Gallery model card 86; standalone comparison entry

alsoCovers.summary: Grouping state-space, grouped attention and expert blocks can keep token mixing separate from per-token routing through a long decoder.
alsoCovers.sequence: Gallery model card 97; standalone comparison entry

alsoCovers.summary: The same recurrent/direct-attention schedule can retain its expert stage across a decoder release.
alsoCovers.sequence: Gallery model card 99; standalone comparison entry

references.dedupeBasis: Repeated gated-state/direct-attention hybrid schedules with independent sparse token updates; repeat counts change, not the mixer or routing roles.

references.summary: A long-context sparse decoder can use recurrent linear mixing most of the time and latent attention at intervals.
references.sequence: Alternative hybrid mixer to figures 25 and 27
references.dedupeBasis: Linear recurrent memory versus latent token history; retain both storage mechanisms.

references.summary: A hybrid mixing schedule can scale up independently of the number of experts available for token updates.
references.sequence: Scaled companion to figure 25
references.dedupeBasis: Fixed hybrid mixer schedule with a changed expert bank/active-capacity comparison.

references.summary: A compact hybrid decoder can use mostly state-space mixing and keep the feed-forward blocks dense.
references.sequence: Dense hybrid counterpart to figure 32

alsoCovers.summary: A hybrid token-mixing schedule can coexist with a dense feed-forward update.
alsoCovers.sequence: Gallery model card 68; standalone comparison entry

references.dedupeBasis: Same state-space/direct-attention mixer pattern with a dense FFN under either mixer.

references.summary: A decoder can change how frequently attention appears at different depths while keeping short convolution and dense token updates.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 75; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Short convolution and periodic grouped attention with dense token updates.

references.summary: Short convolution and grouped attention can both feed a routed per-token update from the start of a decoder.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 77; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Short convolution and grouped attention with expert updates from the opening; distinct from dense updates.

references.summary: A decoder can express position through relative score bias while short convolutions mix nearby tokens inside each block.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 87; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Key/value convolution, relative score bias and separate output convolutions have distinct roles.

references.summary: A dense hybrid may use local convolution, windowed attention, and global attention as three distinct token mixers.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 117; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Local convolution, window attention and global attention each retain a distinct role under a dense FFN.

references.summary: Sparse token selection can replace one attention route while leaving the recurrent mixer and latent expert stages in place.
references.sequence: Gallery model card 119; standalone comparison entry
references.dedupeBasis: Recurrent mixer and latent experts stay fixed while attention switches to indexed selection.
